newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia agency halts October palm oil exports.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia agency halts October palm oil exports.

text.p: Indonesia's joint marketing agency (KPB) has suspended exports of crude palm oil in October to enable it to meet a backlog of previous commitments, a KPB official told Reuters on Wednesday.
"We will not be signing any contracts for October because we want to clear up our previous commitments," the official said, declining to be identified.
The official added that all existing export contracts would however be met.
The official declined to say how many previously-signed contracts had to be met by the agency, through which all crude palm oil produced by state plantations are marketed.
He said 30 percent of the plantations' output were exported, with the rest being channelled into the local market.
State plantations account for about 40 percent of total national production, which amounted to 4.5 million tonnes in 1995 and is forecast to reach 4.9 million tonnes this year.
Traders said there had been market talk that production in some state plantations had been lower than expected.
"There has been talk that production in some state plantations has been poor, especially those in southern Sumatra," one trader said.
But he added that the non-availability of production data made it difficult to verify the rumours.
Another trader said the suspension of October exports by the marketing agency could have an impact on overseas' markets as supply could be squeezed.
"Unless Malaysia steps in to meet the amount of oil that will be missing from the market, supply could tighten," he said. He said the local market was not expected to be affected.
